html:
Ashura is the tenth day of Muharram, the first month of the Islamic calendar. For Shia Muslims it is a day of mourning for Husayn, the grandson of the prophet, who was killed on that day in 680 at the Battle of Karbala.

Shia communities hold processions, sermons and passion plays that retell Husayn's last stand, and many make pilgrimages to his shrine at Karbala. Some mourners beat their chests. The day carries a theme of resisting tyranny at any cost.

For many Sunni Muslims Ashura is a day of voluntary fasting, linked to the prophet's example and to the story of Moses and the Israelites. The same date thus marks a joyful remembrance in one tradition and grief in another. The commemoration is one of the main markers of Shia identity, separate from Sunni practice.
